name: Virtual ANS 3
priceNote: Google Play purchases are blocked for Russia-registered developers since Dec 2024. The developer's site lists workarounds.
description: Simulates the Soviet ANS photoelectronic synthesizer (1938–58). You draw sound as a spectrogram and can convert images to sound and back. MIDI-playable on Android 6+.
whyUnique: You paint sound directly in the frequency domain, a historical instrument rebuilt as an app.
bitwigTips: Export WAV and drop it into Bitwig's Sampler in Spectral or Grains mode for more transformation.

name: SunVox
description: Modular synthesizer combined with a pattern tracker. Also runs on Windows, so projects move between phone and PC.
whyUnique: A deep modular environment and tracker that fits on a phone.
bitwigTips: SunVox also exists for Windows. Finish a pattern on the phone, then render stems for Bitwig.

name: PixiTracker
description: Minimalist, pixel-art sample tracker you can learn in minutes.
whyUnique: The tracker workflow with all the complexity stripped out.
bitwigTips: Use it to sketch loops on the go and export WAV loops for Bitwig's clip launcher.

name: PhonoPaper
description: Encodes sound as printable images (PhonoPaper codes) and plays them back by scanning with the camera.
whyUnique: Sound printed on paper and played with your phone camera.
bitwigTips: Record the camera playback and use the artifacts as textures in Bitwig.

name: Koala Sampler
description: Fast SP-style sampler: record with the mic, chop to pads, and add real-time effects.
whyUnique: Probably the fastest sample-to-beat workflow on Android.
bitwigTips: Export stems or the full beat and drag them into Bitwig. Also try resampling Bitwig loops back into Koala.

name: Caustic 3
description: Rack-style studio with up to 14 machines: synths, drum machines and effects, with a classic hardware feel.
whyUnique: A Reason-style rack on your phone, and still a favorite of mobile producers.
bitwigTips: Export individual machine stems as WAV and rebuild the mix in Bitwig.

name: G-Stomper Studio
description: Drum machine, sampler, VA synths and sequencer in one live-performance studio.
whyUnique: Designed for live performance, unlike most phone DAWs.
bitwigTips: Use Ableton Link (where supported) to sync with Bitwig, or export stems.

name: nanoloop
description: Abstract grid sequencer and synth that started on the Game Boy. Strange at first, very powerful once it clicks.
whyUnique: Its non-linear, minimalist interface steers you toward ideas you wouldn't have otherwise.
bitwigTips: Record the output live into a Bitwig audio track and edit the best takes.

name: Audio Evolution Mobile Studio
description: Full multitrack DAW for Android with USB audio interface support and effects.
whyUnique: The closest thing to a 'real' desktop DAW on Android.
bitwigTips: Export tracks as stems for Bitwig, so the phone works as a portable recording rig.

name: n-Track Studio
description: Multitrack recorder and beat maker that is also available on Windows.
whyUnique: Cross-platform, so phone sessions can continue on your PC.
bitwigTips: Export stems from n-Track and import them into Bitwig.

name: Zenbeats
description: Roland's cross-platform beat-making DAW with classic TR and synth sounds.
whyUnique: Classic Roland sounds on a phone, with projects that move between platforms.
bitwigTips: Export stems to bring those Roland sounds into Bitwig.

name: Remixlive
description: Pad-based loop and sample performance app with effects and recording.
whyUnique: A finger-drumming and loop-launching performance surface, a pocket version of Bitwig's clip launcher.
bitwigTips: Record performances, then drop them into Bitwig and chop with the Sampler.

name: MobMuPlat
description: Runs Pure Data patches on your phone with custom touch interfaces.
whyUnique: Build your own instrument instead of using someone else's.
bitwigTips: Bitwig's Grid shares a patching mindset with Pd. Prototype ideas on either.
